description.narrative:
Projektet syftar till att stärka urbana hälsosystem med fokus på strukturreformer, samordning och partnerskap på nationell nivå. Denna insats som genomförs i samarbete med regeringen i Bangladesh, Sverige och UNICEF, representerar ett steg mot hållbar primärvårdsplanering och service av god kvalitet, särskilt för den fattigaste och mest utsatta delen av befolkningen i urbana områden.
De föreslagna fyra åren (2019-2023) av stöd från UNICEF kommer att fokusera på följande resultat som ska uppnås före 2023: 1. Hälsosystemen stärks genom institutionell reform för en fungerande institutionell struktur och system för datahantering för att förbättra ansvaret för en effektiv primärhälsovård. 2. En innovativ modell för hållbar service upprättas för att förbättra tillgången till och utnyttjandet av primärhälsovård inklusive standardiserade baspaket för nutrition, särskilt för den fattigaste och mest utsatta befolkningen. 3. Förbättrad täckning av primärhälsovård i tätbebyggelse och för socialt segregerade grupper. 4. Evidens på god praxis och lärdomar finns tillgängliga för politisk dialog och för att påverka beslutsprocesser.
Insatsen ska nå 845 000 människor som lever i fattigdom i slumområden eller i andra urbana områden med låg inkomst och som direkt kommer att dra nytta av primärhälsovården. Primärvården avser nå: 1. 45 942 gravida kvinnor för vård vid graviditet och efter förlossning samt förlossningar på vårdinrättning av 32 816 kvinnor 2. 45.942 mödrar till nyfödda får grundläggande vård, 3. 45 492 mödrar får rådgivning om nutrition för mödrar, nyfödda och små barn 4. Vaccinationsprogram till 58 123 barn, genom spårning och kartläggning 5. 20 000 hushåll, ca 100 000 personer, kommer att informeras och uppmuntras att anmäla sig till ett system för grupphälsoförsäkring. 6. 12 000 textilarbetare ska nås av Mother @ Works programmet för att förbättra deras hälso- och näringsstatus samt immunisering. 7. Projektet kommer att bygga upp kapacitet för totalt 540 anställda från nationella till operativa nivåer: (nationella politiska beslutsfattare, hälsovårdsansvariga, leverantörer av hälsovård, sjukvårdspersonal, statsanställda inom vården, kommunala institutioner, icke-statliga organisationer och privat sektor).
Detta ska att uppnås genom en kombination och en balans mellan politisk dialog och påverkansarbete samt utformning av och implementering av vårdprogram.
Primärhälsovården kommer att stärkas genom införandet av ett system för finansiell riskskydd för förbättrad användning och täckning av hälsovård för kvinnor och barn inom utsatta grupper, särskilt de som bor i slumområden. Detta ska bidra till att förbättra efterfrågan, tillgång och användning av kvalitetsservice av mödra- och neonatalvård i marginaliserade områden, och i slutändan uppfylla deras rättigheter till hälsovård och överlevnad. Detta kommer att leda till att en innovativ modell för hållbar service utformas för att förbättra tillgången till och utnyttjandet av primärhälsovård inklusive standardminimipaket för nutrition, särskilt för den fattigaste och mest marginaliserade befolkningen;
En ekonomisk skyddsmekanism genom en grupphälsoförsäkring för låginkomsttagare och socialt segregerade grupper förväntas ge möjlighet till primärhälsovård av kvalitet nära bostaden. I slutändan kommer dessa utsatta och socialt segregerade grupper att ha färre ekonomiska hinder för tillgång till livräddande primärhälsovård; Detta kommer att leda till det förväntade mål 3: Förbättrad täckning av primärhälsovård i tätbebyggelse och för socialt segregerade grupper;
En effektiv policydialog baserad på god praxis och lärdomar från projekt, innovationer och följeforskning, förväntas bidra till engagemang och samordning mellan olika sektorer och avdelningar för en urban primärhälsovård i Bangladesh.
Ett förbättrat styrsystem för urbana hälsoprogram förväntas bidra till att förbättra samordningen, mäta framsteg och ansvarsskyldighet för urban primärvård av de främsta intressenterna, nämligen ministeriet för kommunala frågor, hälsovårdsministeriet och kommunala institutioner. I slutändan kommer stadsbefolkningen, särskilt från marginaliserad områden, bli medvetna om sina rättigheter till hälsovård och välbefinnande.

The project aims at strengthening urban health systems with focus on structural reform, coordination and partnerships at the national level. This proposal, in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh, Government of Sweden and UNICEF, represents a step towards sustainable urban PHC programming for quality health services, especially for the poorest and most vulnerable urban population. The proposed four years ( 2019-2023) of technical assistance from UNICEF will focus on the following results to be achieved by 2023: 1. Health systems are strengthened through institutional reform for functioning institutional structure and data management system to improve accountability for delivery of efficient Primary Health Care (PHC); 2. Innovative model of sustainable service delivery is established to improve access to and utilization of PHC services including standard minimum package of nutrition interventions especially by the poorest and most vulnerable population;3. Improved coverage of PHC in urban slum settlements and for socially segregated groups;4. Evidence on good practices and lessons learned is available for policy dialogue and advocacy to influence decision making processes.One of the most important features of this project is that it benefit 845,000 slum and non slum poor and low income population will benefit from the direct provision of primary health care services in the project areas. This will be achieved through a combination of efforts mix of a balance between upstream policy dialogue and advocacy and downstream work.PHC services will be strengthened through introduction of financial risk protection scheme which will improve the use and coverage of health services by women and children amongst vulnerable populations especially living in slum areas will increase. This will contribute towards improving demand, access and use of quality Maternal Newborn Child and Health services from vulnerable and underserved areas, and ultimately their rights to health care and survival is fulfilled;This will lead to the Innovative model of sustainable service delivery is established to improve access to and utilization of PHC services including standard minimum package of nutrition interventions especially by the poorest and most vulnerable/segregated population;Financial Protection mechanism through group health insurance mechanisms for low income and socially segregated populations will empower to benefit from quality PHC services close to their place of residence. Ultimately these vulnerable and socially segregated populations will experience fewer financial barriers to access life-saving PHC services;This will lead to the expected Objective 3: Improved coverage of PHC in urban slum settlements and for socially segregated groups;The improved governance system of urban health programs will contribute to improving coordination, measuring progress and accountability of urban health service delivery by the primary stakeholders, namely Ministry of Local Government , Ministry of Health and Local Government Institutions. Ultimately the urban population, especially from underserved areas, will realize their rights to health care and well-being.

The overall vision of success for this project is that by 2023, sustainable improvement in the health status of the Bangladeshi population in urban areas is achieved, particularly for the poorest and most vulnerable groups. This will encompass strengthening institutional governance for sustainable delivery of Primary Health Care for women and children amongst the vulnerable population in underserved areas, particularly in urban slums and newly included wards in city corporations and municipalities. The four expected outcomes are:
1. Health systems are strengthened through institutional reform with a functioning institutional structure and data management systems to improve accountability for delivery of efficient Primary Health Care (PHC);2. Innovative model of sustainable service delivery system is established to improve access to and utilization of PHC services especially by the poorest and vulnerable/segregated population ;3. Coverage of primary health care is improved in urban slum settlements and for socially segregated groups4. Evidence based on good practices and lessons learned is available for policy dialogue and advocacy to influence decision making processes.

Annual Narrative Report for the SIDA-funded project Strengthening Urban Health Systems for Comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC) for the Most Deprived Women and Children for the period August 2022 July 2023.
Some of the achievements during the reporting period include:
During the reporting period (1 August 2022 - 30 July 2023),Six urban primary health care clinics (Aalo Clinic) were developed as a comprehensive approach to achieve Universal Health Coverage for the urban population. about 106 000 individual were registered for services in 6 Aalo Clinics and they received about 615K consultations were given from General Practitioners (GPs) and Paramedics of the Clinics out of 600 000 target population. During the same period, 78 000 Lab-tests and 75 000 health screening services were done in Dorgoray Shasthyo (Outreach) of Aalo clinics. One of the Aalo Clinics (Karail) successfully managed an outbreak of Enteric Fever.
10 types of capacity building training courses were conducted for 315 urban health service providers to further strengthen the health system. Besides this, nine different categories of Health Management Information System (HMIS) training courses were conducted among 377 participants. The project supported Health Management Information System (HMIS) of DGHS to include the NGOs involved in health service delivery in urban areas in the national reporting system. A total of 178 out of 190 PHC clinics run by NGOs have regularly started reporting on the essential Maternal Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health and Nutrition (MNCAHN) services in DHIS2. A dashboard has been developed which visualizes the utilization of health care services provided by NGOs and public health facilities under City-Corporations to monitor the performance of health facilities.
UNICEF continuously supports the Urban Health Demographic Surveillance System (UHDSS) to monitor the health service delivery of urban slums and PHC indicators. The information include data on households and population, birth and death, antenatal, post-natal and delivery care, component of ANC, knowledge of danger sign (pregnancy, delivery, postnatal period, and for new-born), knowledge about referral complication (pregnancy and new-born), new-born care, childhood illness, child feeding practices and immunization. Additional social indicators, such as education, occupation, and assets, were added last year. The system provide feedback to understand the health seeking behaviour, coverage, health service utilization and disease profile of the community.
UNICEF initiated a Mothers@Work to improve the coverage of Primary Health Care in terms of maternal and child health and nutrition services for the vulnerable urban dwellers specially for the working mothers from the Ready-Made Garments (RMG) industries and their children. It is being implemented in collaboration with the National Nutrition Services (NNS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE), Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) and in partnership with the private sector (e.g BGMEA and BKMEA) and CSOs. Under this, ten selected RMGs located in the catchment area of the Urban Primary Health Care model clinic (Aalo Clinic) are providing support to the working mothers and their children for antenatal care, nutrition counselling and breastfeeding support. Senior and mid-level management of 10 selected RMGs were sensitised on strengthening MNCAH and Nutrition services by adopting national protocol and guidelines in their PHC centres. This helped create referral linkages with the community based PHC service providers surrounding respective RMG factories to improve access to services by the working mothers and their children.
The market research findings conducted by Implementing Research (IR) Team, showed that in October 2022, only 49 per cent of the respondents were aware of the clinic. In March 2023 reached 73 per cent as indicated by the end-line survey. The total program cost is BDT 95.5 million, where the start-up cost is BDT 23 million (25 per cent) and the implementation cost is BDT 72 million approximately (75 per cent) in a year. The average cost per clinic is BDT 15.9 million on a yearly basis. A Technical Guidance Team is providing guidance to implement the Urban Model PHCs in accordance with the design and identify the scope of improvements that can make the model best fit for the urban context in Bangladesh. The satisfied clients pool has become the prime source for promoting Aalo Clinics in the community.
